capacity_procedure: nested: for every evaluated point and seed, cordonlite.run.calibrate (default bracket and tolerance) is run with that point's behaviour parameters, then the 30-day charged run uses the resulting scale; it targets the car-weighted peak 15-min queue + road delay (engine.calib_delay = 'total') of 15 min

road.status: fixed inputs (config.toml [road], k from data/road_meta.json); not searched

search.method: full factorial grid over PAP and k_WFH in NZ$1 steps, paid parking fixed at NZ$17; nested capacity calibration at every point and seed
search.selection: lexicographic: (1) feasible = every 3-seed mean in its target band at the targets' stated precision (shares to 2 decimals, changes to whole percent) and every seed within the stated single-seed tolerance; (2) among feasible points, the smallest squared relative distance to the anchors (PAP 8 [v3], paid parking 17 [AT car-park all-day rate 2014], k_WFH 8 [v3]); (3) loss as tie-break. If no point is feasible, the lowest loss.
search.loss_doc: Loss of one grid point over its seeds. centre: sum of squared (3-seed mean - centre) / scale for base car, base PT and the d21-30 response (scales 0.05, 0.035, 0.04); band: squared band excess of the 3-seed means for every target (scale 0.02), plus squared excess beyond the stated single-seed tolerance for each seed; prior: 0.02 x sum of squared relative distances of the scalars from the v3 values (8, 8, 8), a weak tie-break toward the design-note values.

gap_sensitivity.reading: The two decisions of 2026-10-05 do different jobs. The SKIP cost removes the postponed trips: with NZ$25 the SKIP share is 0.037 before the charge (0.030, 0.039 and 0.041 on seeds 1-3, all above the 0.02 bound) and 0.092 after it, although the early start is available, and the response (-23.9%) is beyond the band. The early start does not replace postponing in the rule: without it the SKIP share is unchanged (0.002 and 0.014), the point stays feasible, and the 08:00 to 09:00 crossings fall by 37.2% against 21.6% over the whole morning (39.8% and 20.7% with it). How much the early start is used depends on its assumed cost: at NZ$1.5 x phi(F) 13.8% of commuters start early before the charge and 15.4% after it, and the peak crossings fall by 45.8%; at NZ$6 x phi(F) the option is almost unused (0.015, then 0.010). Giving the permission to every employee of the three eligible groups raises the share to 0.104 before and 0.103 after the charge and stays feasible. None of the variants was searched or adopted; 'feasible' is judged at the chosen PAP and k_WFH only.

out_of_sample.note: Out-of-sample checks run after the selection; they did not influence it. Capacity is recalibrated per seed as in the search.

limits: The targets are stated assumptions, and the response anchors are not like-for-like: Stockholm and Gothenburg measured total cordon traffic in charged hours over months to years, while the band here applies to AM car commuters over days 21-30. v3 10.5 asks for a qualitative comparison only; the private-car commuter response is likely larger than the total-traffic one.

Eight of 405 grid points are feasible, all at PAP 22 (k_WFH 9 to 16). At the stated precision base PT is 0.16 at PAP 21 and base car 0.86 to 0.87 at PAP 23 for every k_WFH from 7 to 16, and at PAP 22 a k_WFH of 8 or less gives a days 21-30 response beyond -22% (-23.4% at k_WFH 8). The rule picks PAP 22 / k_WFH 9, the feasible point nearest the anchors, which is also the lowest-loss point of the grid; the search with 300 agents and free-flow roads chose PAP 20 / k_WFH 10. Feasibility is judged at the precision the targets are stated in; on unrounded 3-seed means two points are feasible (k_WFH 9 and 10 at PAP 22), the chosen one among them. Two single-seed values lie outside their band but inside the stated tolerance, both on seed 2: base car 0.856 (0.006 above 0.85) and the days 21-30 response -22.8% (0.8 pp beyond -22%). Every other value is in band (days 21-30: -19.8% and -19.6% on seeds 1 and 3; days 11-13: -25.3%, -29.4%, -26.9%; SKIP 0.001, 0.002, 0.003). The targets were not relaxed.

The response is close to the centre of the band: -20.7% on seeds 1-3 against a centre of -20%, -21.0% on unseen seeds 6-12 (single seeds -19.9% to -23.0%; seed 11 is beyond -22% but within tolerance) and -21.0% over seeds 1-12. Out of sample nothing is outside the stated tolerance, but base car runs high: it is above 0.85 on held-out seed 4 and on unseen seeds 7, 8, 9, 10 and 12 (0.854 to 0.868), and the mean of the unseen seeds 6-12 is 0.856, above the band at the stated precision (over seeds 1-12 it is 0.853, in band). Base PT is above 0.15 on seeds 5 and 11 (0.156, 0.151), within tolerance.

Postponing is rare. With the SKIP cost at NZ$30 plus one hour of VoT the SKIP share is 0.002 before the charge and 0.014 on days 21-30 (seeds 1-3: 0.013, 0.016, 0.013; unseen seeds 6-12: 0.013). The sensitivity runs show that this comes from the SKIP cost and not from the early start: without the early-start option the SKIP share is the same (0.002 and 0.014), and with the SKIP cost back at NZ$25 it is 0.037 before the charge and 0.092 after, even with the early start available.

The charge barely changes how many commuters start early. About 48% may start early; 7.8% of all commuters do so on days 6-10 (9.1% of car users), when the car-weighted peak queue delay is about 5 minutes and the peak queue + road delay about 15. Under the charge the share is 6.6% on days 11-13 and 7.3% on days 21-30, the same as in the no-charge run (7.3%); as a share of the fewer remaining car users it rises to 10.8%. The money saved by crossing early (NZ$4 before 07:30 against NZ$6 from 08:00 to 09:00, plus the loss term) is weighed against the assumed inconvenience of NZ$3 x phi(F), and the result depends on that assumed cost: at NZ$1.5 x phi(F) the share rises under the charge (0.138 to 0.154) and the 08:00 to 09:00 crossings fall by 45.8%; at NZ$6 x phi(F) almost nobody starts early (0.015, then 0.010). The cost and the permission probabilities are assumptions with no empirical source.

Peak spreading is clear in every seed. Car crossings in the 08:00 to 09:00 peak (NZ$6) fall by 39.8% from days 6-10 to days 21-30 against 20.7% over the whole morning (seeds 1-3: 38.9%, 40.0%, 40.5% against 19.8%, 22.8%, 19.6%), and by 42.3% against 21.0% on unseen seeds 6-12 (41.4% against 21.0% over seeds 1-12). Crossings before 07:30 rise by 5.5% on seeds 1-3 (+5.2%, -2.1%, +13.5%) and by 7.5% over seeds 1-12. Against the no-charge run the 08:00 to 09:00 share of crossings falls in every seed (-0.104, -0.084, -0.121) and the 07:00 to 08:00 share rises (+0.083, +0.055, +0.094). In the paired check 32.4% of commuters who drive in both runs have a different modal departure with the charge, 17.9% earlier and 14.5% later (mean shift -6.5 minutes).

Day-to-day churn in the daily rule arm is large: 25% of commuters have a different modal car departure on days 26-30 than on days 6-10 with the charge, and 23% without it. A before-and-after count of retimers therefore says little, and retiming is reported against the no-charge run.

PAP is a fitted residual. With parking and fuel fixed, PAP is the only scalar that can hold the assumed pre-charge split; it is 22 (v3 PAP 22-44 in v3's form, against v3's NZ$8 swept 4-12), up from 20 with 300 agents and free-flow roads. At PAP 22 commuters with P = 1-2 never ride PT (PT share 0.000 in the population manipulation), so PT use is confined to P = 3-5. The baseline shares react sharply to PAP (at k_WFH 9: base PT 0.175 at PAP 20, 0.159 at 21, 0.146 at 22, 0.128 at 23 and 0.116 at 24), while the response depends on it less (-22.0% to -19.4% for PAP 20-24).

k_WFH is identified by the response and overshoot, not by the WFH share: at PAP 22 the days 21-30 response is -23.4% at k_WFH 8, -20.7% at 9, -18.6% at 10 and -15.8% at 12, and the overshoot -29.7%, -27.2%, -24.6% and -21.5%, while base WFH stays below 0.01 (0.007 at k_WFH 8, 0.004 at 9). A realistic hybrid-work baseline is not reproduced: k_WFH 4 gives about 7% WFH before the charge but a response of -31.8%. v3's WFH quota (1-3 days per 5-day block) would bound this margin; it is not implemented.

The fixed inputs carry their own uncertainty. The petrol price (NZ$3.30/L) is author-supplied for October 2026 and was not verified here; the last published figure we read was NZ$2.97/L for September 2026. Consumption is 9.0 L/100 km for every paying driver; electric vehicles, fuel cards and other running costs are not represented. Paid parking NZ$17 is a 2014 casual all-day rate, applied to half of office commuters (the other half park free). The SKIP cost (NZ$30), the early start time (07:00), its cost (NZ$3 x phi(F)) and the permission probabilities (0.8, 0.5, 0, 0.5, 0) are author assumptions. Base years are mixed (2026 fuel, 2025 fare and charge, 2014 parking). The road layer is fixed as well and is not searched: section capacity k = 0.076999 x directional ADT, BPR alpha 0.15 and beta 4 with a speed floor of 0.18, and the motorway breakdown rule (breakdown at V/C 1.0, recovery below 0.95, discharge capacity 10% lower, speed at most 0.45 of free flow).

The v3-valued model (PAP 8, k_WFH 8) with the fixed parking and fuel has base car 0.556 and PT 0.441, far outside the baseline bands, and responds by -30.2% (overshoot -36.4%). Without fuel and with v3's NZ$8 parking (300 agents, free-flow roads) it gave -15.4% (overshoot -25.0%). The scalars were moved to meet the assumed baseline.

The choice depends neither on the soft overshoot bound (the same eight points are feasible, and the same point is chosen, for bounds of -30% to -33%) nor, in this search, on the anchors: the feasible point nearest the anchors is also the lowest-loss point. No other point becomes feasible with the relaxed bound, so the two ridge alternatives checked out of sample are the points nearest the anchors among the ten lowest-loss other points, PAP 21 / k_WFH 9 and 10. They miss feasibility on the rounded base PT share (0.159 and 0.160) and give -21.5% and -19.5% on seeds 4-12 (base PT 0.153 and 0.152), against -21.1% (base PT 0.138) for the chosen point.

Capacity is a further calibrated quantity, recalibrated per point and seed, now against the peak queue + road delay. Its discrete steps add noise to the base shares: at the chosen point the scale is 0.3961 on seeds 1-5 and 0.3646 to 0.4303 on seeds 6-12. The gate queue is the smaller part of the 15-minute target: at the chosen point (seeds 1-3, days 6-10) the car-weighted peak 15-min queue + road delay is 15.5 minutes, the peak of the queue delay alone 5.3 minutes and the mean road delay of a car 7.2 minutes. On days 21-30 the charge brings the peak queue delay down to 1.3 minutes, the peak queue + road delay to 9.5 minutes and the mean road delay to 5.8 minutes.

Single-agent example (tests/test_rules.py): for the shared Layer A with paid parking NZ$17 and the fuel cost of a 20 km path, 250 of the 625 trait combinations ride PT before the charge. Of the other 375, without the early-start permission 315 keep the car at the usual time on the charge morning, 54 switch to PT, 4 retime by 15 minutes (H = 1) and 2 postpone. With the permission 298 keep, 53 switch to PT, 22 leave at 06:30 for the 07:00 start and 2 postpone. The v3 worked example (identical A: pay / PT / retime) still separates only with the v3 settings or with free parking.

H damps the charge wake only at levels 4-5 (days 11-13: -29.8%, -30.7%, -30.5% at H = 1-3, -27.2% and -22.8% at H = 4-5), and not in the long run (-19.9% to -21.3%): habit re-forms on the new mode immediately.

The charge-induced switch to PT is largest at P = 3 (+0.132 against the no-charge run; +0.125 and +0.117 at P = 4-5, 0 at P = 1-2): at P = 4-5 many PT-feasible agents already ride PT without the charge (0.40 and 0.58 of them at days 26-30 in the no-charge run, who-adapts tables). The PT share after the charge rises with P (0.00, 0.00, 0.21, 0.47, 0.58).

The F response gradient (-12.8% at F = 1 to -36.4% at F = 5) still comes mainly from daily WFH of F = 4-5 hybrid workers (no quota; WFH share 0.24 at F = 5 on days 21-30 with the charge). The 08:00 to 09:00 share of crossings falls with F against the no-charge run (+0.011 at F = 1 to -0.208 at F = 5), partly because phi(F) scales the cost of the early day, and retiming of car keepers against the no-charge run is larger at F = 3-5 (+0.127, +0.119, +0.101) than at F = 1-2 (+0.003, +0.054).
Who-adapts tables conditional on being a day-10 driver are biased by selection; the population manipulation is the unbiased check.

The reference fee follows the fee faced, but on car days it uses the fee actually paid (after retiming; v3 uses the fee at h0 before retiming) and alpha 0.3 (SPEC; v3 0.2), so a retimer keeps a loss term on returning to the peak.

The start an option is measured against is chosen from the expected arrival on the morning of the decision and is kept for the outcome: a commuter who planned the 07:00 start and is held up counts as late for 07:00 (and can be woken by T3), not as early for the usual start. For an agent on a standing plan the start is re-read from that morning's expected arrival.

Only the R-daily arm is calibrated, and the clock arms are not run for this report. The LLM deciders are not calibrated, but the shared Layer A inputs (parking, fuel and the early-start permission) reach the LLM prompt. The rule's WFH earns no parking, fuel or commute credit while the prompt states both daily costs, so live-LLM WFH shares are not comparable with the rule arm on this margin, and a live LLM is not told the rule's NZ$3 x phi(F) cost of the early day (it reads the flexibility sentence instead). MockLLM re-weights the same GC parts; its response at the chosen values is not measured here.
